{"parentUuid":"a68ad8a4-5ed1-4830-994b-7fe992a8196f","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"70de699b-7a71-42df-90af-b101bb1aeb0e","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01QzLo5qRMUqbo8Kaej8WwRy","type":"tool_result","content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Turn notes/usage-ledger.csv into a plan-vs-actual budget report.\n\nUsage:\n    uv run python scripts/usage_report.py                 # summary + forecast\n    uv run python scripts/usage_report.py --remaining 4   # 4 tickets still to do\n\nWhy positive deltas: the 5-hour and weekly meters RESET (drop to 0) when their\nwindow rolls over, and the weekly one only ever climbs inside a week. Summing\nonly the increases between consecutive rows measures what you actually spent\nand ignores the resets. That is what spend() does, and it is your exercise.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport csv\nfrom collections import defaultdict\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nLEDGER = Path(\"notes/usage-ledger.csv\")\n\n\ndef spend(series: list[float | None]) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Total rise across a meter that can reset to a lower value.\n\n    Sum every increase between consecutive readings; ignore blanks (None) and\n    any drop, which means the window reset.\n\n    >>> spend([10.0, 12.0, 15.0])\n    5.0\n    >>> spend([80.0, 5.0, 9.0])\n    4.0\n    >>> spend([None, 4.0, None, 7.0])\n    3.0\n    \"\"\"\n    total = 0.0\n    prev: float | None = None\n    for value in series:\n        if value is None:\n            continue\n        if prev is not None and value > prev:\n            total += value - prev\n        prev = value\n    return total\n\ndef read_rows(path: Path) -> list[dict]:\n    with path.open(newline=\"\") as f:\n        return list(csv.DictReader(f))\n\n\ndef to_float(text: str | None) -> float | None:\n    try:\n        return float(text) if text not in (None, \"\") else None\n    except ValueError:\n        return None\n\n\ndef by_phase(rows: list[dict]) -> dict[str, dict]:\n    phases: dict[str, dict] = defaultdict(\n        lambda: {\"turns\": 0, \"five\": [], \"weekly\": [], \"models\": set(), \"providers\": set()}\n    )\n    for row in rows:\n        phase = phases[row.get(\"phase\") or \"unlabelled\"]\n        phase[\"turns\"] += 1\n        phase[\"five\"].append(to_float(row.get(\"five_h_pct\")))\n        phase[\"weekly\"].append(to_float(row.get(\"weekly_pct\")))\n        if row.get(\"model\"):\n            phase[\"models\"].add(row[\"model\"])\n        if row.get(\"provider\"):\n            phase[\"providers\"].add(row[\"provider\"])\n    return phases\n\n\ndef ticket_phases(phases: dict[str, dict]) -> list[str]:\n    return sorted(p for p in phases if p.upper().startswith(\"T\") and p[1:].isdigit())\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    ap.add_argument(\"--ledger\", type=Path, default=LEDGER)","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"9c698084-043d-4aad-82ec-a47c10c7aca5","timestamp":"2026-09-29T03:34:57.024Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Turn notes/usage-ledger.csv into a plan-vs-actual budget report.\n\nUsage:\n    uv run python scripts/usage_report.py                 # summary + forecast\n    uv run python scripts/usage_report.py --remaining 4   # 4 tickets still to do\n\nWhy positive deltas: the 5-hour and weekly meters RESET (drop to 0) when their\nwindow rolls over, and the weekly one only ever climbs inside a week. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\\n\\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\\n\\n## What a good test is\\n\\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \\\"user can checkout with valid cart\\\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\\n\\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\\n\\n## Seams: where tests go\\n\\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\\n\\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\\n\\nAsk: \\\"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\\\"\\n\\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \\\"codebase-design\\\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\\n\\n## Anti-patterns\\n\\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\\n\\n## Rules of the loop\\n\\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\\n\\n\\nARGUMENTS: Implement spend() in scripts/usage_report.py according to Part 5 of the manual. First run tests/test_usage_report.py and confirm the expected failures before editing. Then implement spend() and rerun the tests. Do not change the tests. Write the ticket id into .claude/state/phase \\\"\\n              \\\"at the start of each /implement session.\\\")\\n\\n\\nif __name__ == \\\"__main__\\\":\\n    main()\\n---TESTS---\\n\\\"\\\"\\\"Tests for the token-budget report (IPHS 400 MP2, exercise 2).\\\"\\\"\\\"\\nimport importlib.util\\nimport subprocess\\nimport sys\\nfrom pathlib import Path\\n\\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\\nspec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(\\\"usage_report\\\", ROOT / \\\"scripts\\\" / \\\"usage_report.py\\\")\\nur = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)\\nspec.loader.exec_module(ur)\\n\\nHEADER = \\\"ts,session,phase,provider,model,effort,ctx_pct,five_h_pct,weekly_pct\\\\n\\\"\\n\\n\\ndef ledger(tmp_path, *rows):\\n    p = tmp_path / \\\"usage-ledger.csv\\\"\\n    p.write_text(HEADER + \\\"\\\".join(rows))\\n    return p\\n\\n\\ndef row(phase, five, weekly, model=\\\"Sonnet\\\", provider=\\\"anthropic\\\"):\\n    return f\\\"2026-09-30T10:00:00Z,abc,{phase},{provider},{model},medium,40.0,{five},{weekly}\\\\n\\\"\\n\\n\\ndef test_spend_counts_only_increases():\\n    assert ur.spend([10.0, 12.0, 15.0]) == 5.0\\n\\n\\ndef test_spend_ignores_window_reset():\\n    assert ur.spend([80.0, 5.0, 9.0]) == 4.0\\n\\n\\ndef test_spend_skips_blanks():\\n    assert ur.spend([None, 4.0, None, 7.0]) == 3.0\\n\\n\\ndef test_spend_empty_is_zero():\\n    assert ur.spend([]) == 0.0 and ur.spend([None, None]) == 0.0\\n\\n\\ndef test_report_groups_by_phase(tmp_path):\\n    p = ledger(tmp_path, row(\\\"grill\\\", 5, 2, model=\\\"Opus\\\"), row(\\\"grill\\\", 15, 6, model=\\\"Opus\\\"),\\n               row(\\\"T01\\\", 20, 8), row(\\\"T01\\\", 30, 12))\\n    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / \\\"scripts/usage_report.py\\\"),\\n                          \\\"--ledger\\\", str(p)], capture_output=True, text=True)\\n    assert \\\"grill\\\" in out.stdout and \\\"10.0%\\\" in out.stdout   # 5 -> 15\\n    assert \\\"Opus\\\" in out.stdout\\n    assert \\\"average weekly cost per ticket: 4.0%\\\" in out.stdout\\n\\n\\ndef test_forecast_flags_over_budget(tmp_path):\\n    p = ledger(tmp_path, row(\\\"T01\\\", 10, 60), row(\\\"T01\\\", 40, 80))\\n    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / \\\"scripts/usage_report.py\\\"),\\n                          \\\"--ledger\\\", str(p), \\\"--remaining\\\", \\\"4\\\"], capture_output=True, text=True)\\n    assert \\\"OVER BUDGET\\\" in out.stdout and \\\"split fat tickets\\\" in out.stdout\\n\\n\\ndef test_missing_ledger_explains(tmp_path):\\n    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / \\\"scripts/usage_report.py\\\"),\\n                          \\\"--ledger\\\", str(tmp_path / \\\"nope.csv\\\")], capture_output=True, text=True)\\n    assert out.returncode != 0 and \\\"Stop hook\\\" in out.stderr\\n\\n\\ndef test_backup_provider_shown(tmp_path):\\n    p = ledger(tmp_path, row(\\\"T05\\\", 0, 10, model=\\\"glm-5.3\\\", provider=\\\"api.z.ai\\\"),\\n               row(\\\"T05\\\", 5, 14, model=\\\"glm-5.3\\\", provider=\\\"api.z.ai\\\"))\\n    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / \\\"scripts/usage_report.py\\\"),\\n                          \\\"--ledger\\\", str(p)], capture_output=True, text=True)\\n    assert \\\"@api.z.ai\\\" in out.stdout\",\"is_error\":false}]},\"uuid\":\"c310e538-fb83-4d06-99bd-9a66ab235602\",\"timestamp\":\"2026-09-29T02:31:30.002Z\",\"toolUseResult\":{\"stdout\":\"#!/usr/bin/env python3\\n\\\"\\\"\\\"Turn notes/usage-ledger.csv into a plan-vs-actual budget report.\\n\\nUsage:\\n    uv run python scripts/usage_report.py                 # literal text on render — the real\n   security boundary), and `sanitize_markdown_source` was replaced with a\n   narrow regex strip of `<script>`/`<style>` blocks and `on*` event\n   attributes, which doesn't touch entities. Added\n   `test_saving_plain_text_does_not_corrupt_it` as a regression test.\n\n2. **`app/db.py:24` — permanent-page slugs duplicated (SQL `CHECK` vs. Python\n   tuple).** The three slugs were hardcoded separately in the schema's `CHECK`\n   constraint and in `PAGE_SLUGS`, risking drift if a page were ever\n   added/renamed. **Fixed:** `PAGE_SLUGS` is now the single source of truth —\n   the `CHECK` clause is generated from it when building `SCHEMA`.\n\nFull test suite: 35 passed (6 new in `tests/test_pages.py`, matching the\nticket's required coverage: admin edit success, editor-blocked UI + direct\nPOST, anonymous-redirected, sanitization of a script/onerror payload, plus\nthe entity-corruption regression above).\nEOF\n)\"\n","description":"Post code-review findings and resolutions as a comment on issue #3"}},"wireIngestContext":{"toolu_01NvsLorXokGPzvxaKx9tbRS":{"cwd":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms"}},"serverClassifierRequest":"95d28c0a-40bb-47ba-b9fd-8a971675ccc1","apiBlockIndex":2,"requestId":"req_011CfX2ixFpRCY2f87zYSLuB","type":"assistant","uuid":"4db78e75-3682-4ba7-ac6d-2b16079c5108","timestamp":"2026-09-29T03:36:04.184Z","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"a2316d11-3941-4d87-98fe-7d21dea1d9fa","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"2fa5b7df-506f-4d8e-a53d-7174fd72d15b","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"87de0628-4545-40db-9ddf-94f88489f428","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfX2nECraD1wMKjNiEPxT","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Committed and closed ticket #3. Here's the summary:\n\n## What was built\n- `pages` table (`app/db.py`) for Home/Menu/Our Story with title, Markdown body, status, author, timestamps.\n- `app/content.py`: Markdown rendering with raw HTML disabled (the real XSS boundary) plus a targeted strip of `<script>`/`<style>`/`on*` attributes on save.\n- `app/routes/pages.py`: `/admin/pages` and `/admin/pages/{slug}` — Manager-only, with role checks that run *before* CSRF checks so a hand-crafted POST is blocked by role, not just missing UI.\n- Seeded Home/Menu/Our Story content sourced from `notes/restaurant-research.md`, with clearly labeled placeholders for the one unverified fact (phone number) and photos.\n- `tests/test_pages.py` (7 tests): admin edit success, editor blocked on UI and direct POST, anonymous redirected to login, script/onerror sanitization, and a regression test for an entity-corruption bug caught in review.\n\n## Code review\n`/code-review medium` found two real issues, both fixed:\n1. Sanitizing raw Markdown with `nh3.clean()` HTML-entity-encoded plain text (`&` → `&amp;`), corrupting content every save/reload — fixed by disabling raw HTML in the renderer and switching to a narrow regex-based source strip.\n2. Permanent-page slugs were duplicated between a SQL `CHECK` and a Python tuple — fixed by generating the `CHECK` clause from `PAGE_SLUGS`.\n\nFindings + resolutions posted to [issue #3](https://github.com/algoal0507-crypto/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/3#issuecomment-5883132805). Full suite: **35 passed**.\n\n## Usage report (not previously recorded)\n```\nphase          turns  5h spent   weekly  models / provider\nT01                3      3.0%     0.0%  Sonnet 5\nT03                1      0.0%     0.0%  Sonnet 5   ← stray label, see note below\nunlabelled        20     13.0%     2.0%  Sonnet 5\n\nTickets done: 2 · average weekly cost per ticket: 0.0%\nForecast: 6 tickets need ~0% of the weekly cap; 95% remains → FITS\n```\nNote: I briefly wrote `T03` to `.claude/state/phase` by mistake early in this session before correcting it to `T02` (ticket #3's actual id). That produced one stray `T03` row in the ledger — harmless, but flagging it since the ledger is append-only and I didn't edit it after the fact.\n\n## Preview locally\n```bash\nuv run cms serve\n```\nThen in a browser:\n1. Go to `http://localhost:8000/login`, sign in as the Manager (`manager@laoncemil.test`, password from your `.env`'s `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`).\n2. From the dashboard, click **\"Edit permanent pages\"**, or go directly to `http://localhost:8000/admin/pages`.\n3. Click Home, Menu, or Our Story to edit — the form shows a live-rendered sanitized preview below the editor.\n\nIf your database doesn't have the seeded content yet, run `uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py` first (requires `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`/`CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD` in `.env`)."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":922,"cache_read_input_tokens":137849,"output_tokens":1174,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":922,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1174,"cache_read_input_tokens":137849,"cache_creation_input_tokens":922,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":922},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"d4809c92-b1ed-4e9a-9cc4-8ba4cdea438c","apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011CfX2nDo3vFtoyV3Wt4ZjK","type":"assistant","uuid":"680bdca8-0095-4635-b949-e611c9cff3a1","timestamp":"2026-09-29T03:36:46.034Z","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"a2316d11-3941-4d87-98fe-7d21dea1d9fa","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"2fa5b7df-506f-4d8e-a53d-7174fd72d15b","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"main"}

Students see the same checklist the judge uses.\n**Repos:** students copy the public template `jon-chun/iphs400-mp2-cms-starter`; all grading artifacts stay in the private `jon-chun/iphs400-mp2-cms-starter-dev`.\n\n> **Policy.** MP2 is **Pass/No-Pass at 5% of the course grade**. **≥70 = Pass**, **<70 = No-Pass**.\n> Extra credit counts **only if the score is ≥70 without it**; it can raise a Pass, never create one.\n> Under 70, or flagged: one resubmission within one week of feedback, up to full credit.\n> Solo project. Every commit after the template's base commit must be authored by the student.\n\n---\n\n## Part I — The Rubric\n\n### 1. What you submit\n\n| Stage | Deadline (Eastern, EDT, UTC−4) | Tag | Email subject |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **Stage 1 — MVP** | Soft target: **Tue Sep 29, 2026, 2:40 pm** | `mp2-mvp` | `IPHS400 MP2 Stage 1 — {First Last}` |\n| **Stage 2 — Full CMS** | **Tue Oct 6, 2026, 2:40 pm**; no-penalty grace until **Wed Oct 7, 2:40 pm** | `mp2-final` | `IPHS400 MP2 Stage 2 — {First Last}` |\n\nEmail body, both stages: repo URL, GitHub Pages URL, tag name. Stage 2 also attaches the report.\nStage 1 is soft: its 15 points count whenever `mp2-mvp` exists before the Stage 2 deadline. The 48-hour feedback promise applies only to Stage 1 submissions made on time.\n\n**Required artifacts** (all checked by `scripts/check_submission.py`, which the judge runs first; run it yourself before submitting):\n\n| Artifact | Location |\n|---|---|\n| CMS field notes | `notes/cms-field-notes.md` |\n| Glossary and decisions | `CONTEXT.md`, `docs/adr/` |\n| Spec | GitHub issue labeled `spec` |\n| Tickets | GitHub issues labeled `ticket` (core) or `stretch`, with \"Blocked by\" lines |\n| Code-review findings | A comment on each ticket issue, posted before it closes |\n| Handoffs | `docs/handoff/{NN}_{purpose}_{YYYYMMDD}.md` |\n| Session transcripts | `docs/transcripts/iphs400_mp2-cms_chat-session_{NN}_{first}-{last}_{YYYYMMDD}.md` |\n| Compaction log | `docs/process/compaction-log.md` |\n| Token budget | `notes/token-budget-plan.md`, `notes/usage-ledger.csv` |\n| Demo data | `scripts/seed_demo.py`, `.env.example` |\n| Screenshots | `docs/screenshots/` — login, dashboard, content list, editor, users, editor-denied; each at 1280 px and 390 px |\n| Report | `docs/iphs400_mp2-web-cms_report_{first}-{last}_{YYYYMMDD}.md` (same file attached to the Stage 2 email) |\n| README | Sections: *Live URL*, *Run locally*, *Generative AI Use Statement* (with a *Backends used* table) |\n| Published site | `gh-pages` branch, served at the Pages URL |\n\n**The 7 required capabilities** (your client's names may differ, e.g. \"announcements\" for posts):\n\n1. **Login.** Admins and editors log in and out; passwords are hashed.\n2. **Roles.** Two roles, *admin* and *editor*, with different permissions.\n3. **Posts.** Create, read, update, delete; title, slug, Markdown body, status *draft*/*published*, author, timestamps.\n4. **Pages.** Same fields and operations as posts, plus appearing in the public navigation.\n5. **Admin console.** Dashboard, filterable content list, editor with preview.\n6. **User management.** Admin only: create users, change roles, deactivate.\n7. **Public site and publish.** Published content only, sanitized Markdown, nav built from pages; `cms publish` exports to Pages with relative paths.\n\n### 2. How scoring works\n\n- **Every point is a checklist item** with a stated measure and a stated way to check it. {"parentUuid":"c00d168d-6685-4d79-82b8-8be5eb82d560","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"709d2648-a612-4116-b647-bf3a42365b27","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01QqsD5QML2EkYXBFx6hFa2n","type":"tool_result","content":"23. As the Editor, I want the user-management routes to be unreachable to me (no UI\n    entry point, and a 403/redirect on direct request), so that only the Manager\n    controls accounts.\n24. As a visitor, I want the public Home page to show verified address, hours, a\n    directions link, and a prominent Call button, prioritized above other content\n    (signature dish, walk-in-only note), so that I get the \"where and when\" answer\n    immediately.\n25. As a visitor, I want the public site to show only published content — no draft\n    ever appears — so that I never see unfinished or unreviewed material.\n26. As a visitor, I want any Markdown-authored content (News, Home, Menu, Our Story)\n    to render safely, with scripts and dangerous attributes stripped, so that the\n    public site can't be used to inject malicious content even if a draft author\n    pasted something unsafe.\n27. As a visitor, I want every link and asset on the exported site to use a relative\n    path (never root-absolute), so that the site works correctly when served from a\n    GitHub Pages project subfolder.\n28. As a visitor, I want every published page — including Home — reachable by\n    clicking through the site's navigation, so that no published content is an\n    unlinked orphan.\n29. As the Manager, I want `cms publish` to regenerate `site/` from only the current\n    published content, so that unpublishing something and re-running publish actually\n    removes it from the export.\n30. As the Manager, I want a News post to include one real, dated Michelin star\n    announcement (attributed to the Lomas de Chapultepec address, matching the\n    Michelin Guide's own attribution) alongside clearly labeled demo announcements, so\n    that the demo doesn't read as entirely fictional while staying honest about what's\n    invented.\n31. As anyone viewing any seed/demo content, I want a clear label distinguishing real,\n    sourced content from invented sample content, so that the site never implies La\n    Once Mil created or endorsed this project.\n32. As the grader/developer, I want two seeded demo accounts (\"Demo Manager\",\n    \"Demo Editor\") that are clearly fictional and not tied to the real owner's\n    identity, so that both roles are testable without misrepresenting real staff.\n33. As the Manager, I want the Menu page to be one ordinary Markdown page listing dish\n    names and descriptions with no prices, so that I never publish an unverified peso\n    price.\n34. As a visitor, I want image placeholders (e.g. `[PLACEHOLDER: storefront photo]`)\n    to render as clearly labeled placeholders rather than broken image tags, so that\n    missing photography doesn't look like a bug.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Roles**: two enforced roles, `admin` (\"Manager\" in client-facing copy) and\n  `editor`. Role is a column on the user record, checked server-side on every\n  state-changing and every admin-only read route — never enforced only by hiding UI.\n- **Permission matrix**:\n  - `admin`: create/edit/delete/publish News; create/edit permanent pages (Home,\n    Menu, Our Story); create/edit-role/deactivate users; view dashboard and full\n    content list.\n  - `editor`: create/edit News as drafts only (cannot set status to published, cannot\n    delete a published post); cannot reach permanent-page editors or user-management\n    routes (403/redirect on both UI and direct request); can view the dashboard and\n    content list scoped to what they're allowed to act on.\n- **Content types**: `Post` (News) and `Page` (Home, Menu, Our Story) share the same\n  field set — title, slug, Markdown body, status (`draft`/`published`), author\n  (foreign key to user), created/updated timestamps. `Page` additionally participates\n  in the public navigation once published; `Post` (News) is listed reverse-chronological\n  on a News index.\n- **Permanent pages are fixed, not freely creatable**: exactly three Page records\n  (Home, Menu, Our Story) exist for this client — creating a fourth arbitrary Page is\n  out of scope (see Out of Scope). Home is not a nav entry itself (it's the entry\n  point); Menu and Our Story are.\n- **Publish/export boundary (ADR-001)**: \"published\" is a status flag in the local\n  SQLite database — it does not touch the public site. `cms publish` (via\n  `render_site()` in `app/publish.py`) reads only `status = published` rows, renders\n  Markdown through the sanitizer, and writes `site/` with one file per published item\n  plus a News index and nav links built from published Pages. `cms deploy` pushes\n  `site/` to `gh-pages`. TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,\n    role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pages (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    title TEXT NOT NULL,\n    body_md TEXT (datetime('now')),\n    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n);\n\"\"\"\n\nSLUG_PATTERN = \"^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$\"\n\n\ndef get_connection(path: Path | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(path or settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    return conn\n\n\ndef init_db(path: Path | None = None) -> None:\n    conn = get_connection(path)\n    try:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n        for slug in PAGE_SLUGS:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT OR IGNORE INTO pages (slug, title) VALUES (?, ?)\",\n                (slug, PAGE_TITLES[slug]),\n            )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef create_user(email: str, password: str, role: str, *, active: bool = True) -> None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO users (email, password_hash, role, active) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (email, auth.hash_password(password), role, int(active)),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef get_user_by_email(email: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?\", (email,)\n        ).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef get_user_by_id(user_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?\", (user_id,)\n        ).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef set_active(email: str, *, active: bool) -> None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE users SET active = ? response.headers[\"location\"].endswith(\"/login\")","originalFile":"\"\"\"T02: Pages (create/read/update/delete), seeded with Home, Menu, Our Story.\n\nPer the MP2 rubric/manual, Pages support the (UI and a hand-crafted direct POST/DELETE), an anonymous visitor\nredirected to login, and Markdown sanitization of a script/onerror payload.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom app import db\n\n\ndef _csrf(client, path):\n    response = client.get(path)\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n    return response.cookies[\"csrf_token\"]\n\n\ndef test_manager_can_edit_a_permanent_page(client_as):\n    manager = client_as(\"admin\")\n    csrf = _csrf(manager, \"/admin/pages/home\")\n    response = manager.post(\n        \"/admin/pages/home\",\n        data={\n            \"title\": \"Home\",\n            \"body_md\": \"Visit us at Monte Everest 780, Lomas de Chapultepec.\",\n            \"status\": \"published\",\n            \"csrf_token\": csrf,\n        },\n    )\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n    page = db.get_page_by_slug(\"home\")\n    assert page[\"status\"] == \"published\"\n    assert \"Monte Everest 780\" in page[\"body_md\"]\n    assert page[\"author_id\"] is not None\n\n\ndef test_editor_is_blocked_from_edit_form(client_as):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    response = editor.get(\"/admin/pages/home\", follow_redirects=False)\n    assert response.status_code == 403\n\n\ndef test_editor_is_blocked_from_pages_list(client_as):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    response = editor.get(\"/admin/pages\", follow_redirects=False)\n    assert response.status_code == 403\n\n\ndef test_editor_is_blocked_from_a_direct_post(client_as):\n    \"\"\"A forged POST with no prior UI visit must still be rejected by role,\n    not merely by a missing CSRF token.\"\"\"\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    response = editor.post(\n        \"/admin/pages/home\",\n        data={\"title\": \"Hijacked\", \"body_md\": \"x\", \"status\": \"published\",\n              \"csrf_token\": \"not-even-a-real-token\"},\n        follow_redirects=False,\n    )\n    assert response.status_code == 403\n    assert db.get_page_by_slug(\"home\")[\"title\"] != \"Hijacked\"\n\n\ndef test_anonymous_is_redirected_to_login(client):\n    response = payload = '<script>alert(1)</script><img src=x onerror=\"alert(2)\">Tacos al pastor'\n    response = manager.post(\n        \"/admin/pages/menu\",\n        data={\"title\": \"Menu\", \"body_md\": assert \"onerror\" not in page[\"body_md\"]\n    assert \"Tacos al pastor\" in page[\"body_md\"]\n\n    assert \"<script\" not in response.text\n    assert \"onerror\" not in response.text\n\n\ndef Deactivated users fail\n160\t  login with a clear rejection message even with the correct password, and any\n161\t  existing session for that user is treated as invalid on the next authenticated\n162\t  request.\n163\t- **Seed data** (`scripts/seed_demo.py`): creates exactly two users, \"Demo Manager\"\n164\t  (admin) and \"Demo Editor\" (editor), with passwords read from the environment\n165\t  (`.env.example` documents the variable names) — never hard-coded, never the real\n166\t  owner's name. Seeds the three permanent pages (Home/Menu/Our Story, published) and\n167\t  a small set of News posts: one real dated item (the Michelin star announcement,\n168\t  attributed to the Lomas de Chapultepec address) plus additional clearly-labeled\n169\t  demo announcements (e.g. a `[DEMO CONTENT]` marker in the body or a dedicated\n170\t  \"demo\" flag rendered as a badge).\n171\t- **Images**: no upload/media-library feature in this spec (that's the \"Media uploads\"\n172\t  stretch goal). Placeholder images are literal labeled text/markup\n173\t  (`[PLACEHOLDER: storefront photo]`) embedded in seed content, rendered as visible\n174\t  placeholder blocks, not broken `<img>` tags.\n175\t- **Modules to build** (new, under `app/`): `app/models.py` or `app/db.py` (SQLite\n176\t  schema: users, pages, posts), `app/auth.py` (login/session/CSRF/role-check\n177\t  helpers), `app/routes/auth.py`, `app/routes/posts.py`, `app/routes/pages.py`,\n178\t  `app/routes/users.py`, `app/routes/admin.py` (dashboard/content list), each\n179\t  `include_router`'d from `app/main.py` per its existing comment. `app/publish.py`\n180\t  extends `render_site()` to iterate published Posts/Pages instead of the current\n181\t  hard-coded empty-items placeholder.\n182\t\n183\t## Testing Decisions\n184\t\n185\t- Tests only assert on external behavior — HTTP status/redirect/response body for the\n186\t  HTTP seam, and files/content under `site/` for the export seam. No test reaches into\n187\t  the database or calls an internal function to check state a real user/visitor\n188\t  couldn't observe.\n189\t- **Seam 1 — HTTP** (`client`, `client_as` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py`,\n190\t  prior art: `tests/test_t00.py`): login success/failure/logout; anonymous access to\n191\t  any admin route redirects to login; `client_as(\"editor\")` gets 403/redirect on\n192\t  every admin-only route (permanent-page edit, publish action, user management) —\n193\t  including a direct POST that bypasses the UI entirely, matching the \"editors cannot\n194\t  bypass restrictions by submitting requests directly\" requirement; Editor CRUD on\n195\t  News is confined to draft status; Manager can publish/unpublish; dashboard and\n196\t  content-list filters return the expected counts/subsets; user creation, role\n197\t  change, and deactivation each work only for the admin client; a deactivated user's\n198\t  login is refused and, if feasible to simulate, their existing session stops\n199\t  authenticating on the next request.\n200\t- **Seam 2 — Export** (`render_site()` in `app/publish.py`, prior art:\n201\t  `tests/test_t00.py`'s two existing publish rendered in the admin preview — both surfaces sanitize, not just the export.\n- **Sessions**: signed session cookies (`itsdangerous`, already pinned) carrying user\n  id and role; no client-side role trust — every request re-checks role from the\n  session-resolved user record so a deactivated user's existing session stops working\n  on the next request, not just at next login.\n- **Password storage**: argon2 (`argon2-cffi`, already pinned) hashes only; plaintext\n  is never stored or logged.\n- **CSRF**: every state-changing form (login excluded, since it has no prior session)\n  carries a CSRF token validated server-side before the action runs.\n- **Deactivation**: a boolean/status flag on the user record. Deactivated users fail\n  login with a clear rejection message even with the correct password, and any\n  existing session for that user is treated as invalid on the next authenticated\n  request.\n- **Seed data** (`scripts/seed_demo.py`): creates exactly two users, \"Demo Manager\"\n  (admin) and \"Demo Editor\" (editor), with passwords read from the environment\n  (`.env.example` documents the variable names) — never hard-coded, never the real\n  owner's name. Seeds the three permanent pages (Home/Menu/Our Story, published) and\n  a small set of News posts: one real dated item (the Michelin star announcement,\n  attributed to the Lomas de Chapultepec address) plus additional clearly-labeled\n  demo announcements (e.g. a `[DEMO CONTENT]` marker in the body or a dedicated\n  \"demo\" flag rendered as a badge).\n- **Images**: no upload/media-library feature in this spec (that's the \"Media uploads\"\n  stretch goal). Placeholder images are literal labeled text/markup\n  (`[PLACEHOLDER: storefront photo]`) embedded in seed content, rendered as visible\n  placeholder blocks, not broken `<img>` tags.\n- **Modules to build** (new, under `app/`): `app/models.py` or `app/db.py` (SQLite\n  schema: users, pages, posts), `app/auth.py` (login/session/CSRF/role-check\n  helpers), `app/routes/auth.py`, `app/routes/posts.py`, `app/routes/pages.py`,\n  `app/routes/users.py`, `app/routes/admin.py` (dashboard/content list), each\n  `include_router`'d from `app/main.py` per its existing comment. `app/publish.py`\n  extends `render_site()` to iterate published Posts/Pages instead of the current\n  hard-coded empty-items placeholder.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- Tests only assert on external behavior — HTTP status/redirect/response body for the\n  HTTP seam, and files/content under `site/` for the export seam. No test reaches into\n  the database or calls an internal function to check state a real user/visitor\n  couldn't observe.\n- **Seam 1 — HTTP** (`client`, `client_as` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py`,\n  prior art: `tests/test_t00.py`): login success/failure/logout; anonymous access to\n  any admin route redirects to login; `client_as(\"editor\")` gets 403/redirect on\n  every admin-only route (permanent-page edit, publish action, user management) —\n  including a direct POST that bypasses the UI entirely, matching the \"editors cannot\n  bypass restrictions by submitting requests directly\" requirement; Editor CRUD on\n  News is confined to draft status; Manager can publish/unpublish; dashboard and\n  content-list filters return the expected counts/subsets; user creation, role\n  change, and deactivation each work only for the admin client; a deactivated user's\n  login is refused and, if feasible to simulate, their existing session stops\n  authenticating on the next request.\n- **Seam 2 — Export** (`render_site()` in `app/publish.py`, prior art:\n  `tests/test_t00.py`'s two existing publish tests): a draft never appears in any file\n  under `site/`; a `<script>`/`onerror=` payload saved in a post's body does not\n  survive into the exported HTML unescaped/executable; every `href=`/`src=` in the\n  exported output is relative, never root-absolute; Home, Menu, and\nOur Story are La Once Mil's starting content — not a ceiling on what a Manager\ncan do.\n\n**Resolved:**\n- Removed the `CHECK (slug IN (...))` constraint; `pages.slug` is now just\n  `UNIQUE`.\n- Added `db.create_page`/`db.delete_page` and `db.slug_is_valid` (lowercase\n  letters/digits/hyphens).\n- Added `GET/POST /admin/pages/new` (create) and\n  `POST /admin/pages/{slug}/delete` — Manager-only, same role/CSRF checks as\n  edit, invalid slug and duplicate-slug both rejected with a 400 and the form\n  re-shown.\n- `init_db` now seeds the three starting pages only when the `pages` table is\n  empty, so deleting one doesn't resurrect it on the next `cms serve` restart.\n- Updated spec issue #1: replaced the \"fixed, not freely creatable\" decision\n  and the matching Out-of-Scope line with the corrected CRUD decision.\n- Added 7 new tests: create success, duplicate-slug rejection, invalid-slug\n  rejection, delete success, Editor blocked from create/delete (UI + direct\n  POST), anonymous redirected from create/delete.\n\nFull suite: **41 passed** (13 in `tests/test_pages.py`).\nEOF\n)\"\n","description":"Post the CRUD scope-correction findings and resolution to issue #3"}},"wireIngestContext":{"toolu_019LfiUvz9Ezv49C6SUTJN8U":{"cwd":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms"}},"serverClassifierRequest":"4e4f491f-7fc2-42a5-a33c-914a055cbb92","apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CfX3BQLChsq1PAagP7EbK","type":"assistant","uuid":"f987fb70-3ed0-41c6-a334-4e0ac59b3716","timestamp":"2026-09-29T03:41:59.179Z","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"a2316d11-3941-4d87-98fe-7d21dea1d9fa","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"2fa5b7df-506f-4d8e-a53d-7174fd72d15b","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"main"}

Summary:\n\n**Mismatch found:** the rubric and manual both require Pages to support \"the same fields and operations as posts\" — full CRUD — but the implementation (following spec #1's \"fixed, not freely creatable\" decision) only allowed editing three hardcoded slugs via a SQL `CHECK` constraint.\n\n**Resolved:**\n- Dropped the slug `CHECK` constraint; added `db.create_page`/`db.delete_page`/`db.slug_is_valid`.\n- Added `GET/POST /admin/pages/new` and `POST /admin/pages/{slug}/delete`, with the same Manager-only role+CSRF enforcement as edit (editor blocked with 403 on UI and forged direct requests; See ADR-002 for why\nthere is no ORM here.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom app import auth, settings\n\n# La Once Mil's initial Pages (see notes/restaurant-research.md); this is\n# seed content, not a limit. Per the MP2 rubric/manual (\"Pages: same fields\n# and operations as posts, plus public navigation\"), Pages support full\n# create/read/update/delete like Posts — the Manager can add or remove pages\n# beyond this starting set.\nPAGE_SLUGS = (\"home\", \"menu\", \"our-story\")\nPAGE_TITLES = {\"home\": \"Home\", \"menu\": \"Menu\", \"our-story\": \"Our Story\"}\n\nSCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,\n    role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pages (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    title TEXT NOT NULL,\n    body_md TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')) DEFAULT 'draft',\n    author_id INTEGER REFERENCES users(id),\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n);\n\"\"\"\n\nSLUG_PATTERN = \"^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$\"\n\n\ndef get_connection(path: Path | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(path or settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    return conn\n\n\ndef init_db(path: Path | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Create the schema and, only on a brand-new database, seed the\n    starting Pages. Pages are freely creatable/deletable (see PAGE_SLUGS'\n    docstring), so this must not resurrect a page the Manager deleted —\n    it only bootstraps an empty table, never re-inserts into a populated one.\n    \"\"\"\n    conn = get_connection(path)\n    try:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n        if conn.execute(\"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pages\").fetchone()[0] == 0:\n            for slug in PAGE_SLUGS:\n                conn.execute(\n                    \"INSERT INTO pages (slug, title) VALUES (?, ?)\",\n                    (slug, PAGE_TITLES[slug]),\n                )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef create_user(email: str, password: str, role: str, *, active: bool = True) -> None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO users (email, password_hash, role, active) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (email, auth.hash_password(password), role, int(active)),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef get_user_by_email(email: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?\", (email,)\n        ).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef get_user_by_id(user_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?\", (user_id,)\n        ).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef set_active(email: str, *, active: bool) -> None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE users SET active = ? WHERE email = ?\", (int(active), email)\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef get_page_by_slug(slug: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM pages WHERE slug = ?\", (slug,)\n        ).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef list_pages() -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM pages ORDER BY slug\").fetchall()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef update_page(slug: str, *, title: str, body_md: str, status: str, author_id: int) -> None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"\"\"UPDATE pages\n               SET title = ?, body_md = ?, status = ?, author_id = ?,\n                   updated_at = datetime('now')\n               WHERE slug = ?\"\"\",\n            (title, body_md, status, author_id, slug),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef slug_is_valid(slug: str) -> bool:\n    return re.fullmatch(SLUG_PATTERN, slug) is not None\n\n\ndef create_page(slug: str, *, title: str, body_md: str, status: str, author_id: int) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Insert a new page. Returns False if the slug is already taken.\"\"\"\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO pages (slug, title, body_md, status, author_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (slug, title, body_md, status, author_id),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n        return True\n    except sqlite3.IntegrityError:\n        return False\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef delete_page(slug: str) -> None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM pages WHERE slug = ?\", (slug,))\n        conn.commit()\n See ADR-002 for why\nthere is no ORM here.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom app import auth, settings\n\n# La Once Mil's initial Pages (see notes/restaurant-research.md); this is\n# seed content, not a limit. Per the MP2 rubric/manual (\"Pages: same fields\n# and operations as posts, plus public navigation\"), Pages support full\n# create/read/update/delete like Posts — the Manager can add or remove pages\n# beyond this starting set.\nPAGE_SLUGS = (\"home\", \"menu\", \"our-story\")\nPAGE_TITLES = {\"home\": \"Home\", \"menu\": \"Menu\", \"our-story\": \"Our Story\"}\n\nUSERS_SCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,\n    role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1\n);\n\"\"\"\n\nPAGES_SCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pages (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    title TEXT NOT NULL,\n    body_md TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')) DEFAULT 'draft',\n    author_id INTEGER REFERENCES users(id),\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n);\n\"\"\"\n\nSCHEMA = USERS_SCHEMA + PAGES_SCHEMA\n\nSLUG_PATTERN = \"^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$\"\n\n_PAGE_COLUMNS = \"id, slug, title, body_md, status, author_id, created_at, updated_at\"\n\n\ndef _migrate_legacy_page_slug_check(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A database created before Pages supported full CRUD has\n    `CHECK (slug IN ('home', 'menu', 'our-story'))` baked into the `pages`\n    table — `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` never touches an existing table, so\n    that CHECK would otherwise survive forever and silently block creating\n    any other page. Rebuild the table from PAGES_SCHEMA, keeping every row.\n    \"\"\"\n    row = conn.execute(\n        \"SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'pages'\"\n    ).fetchone()\n    if row is None or row[0] is None or \"CHECK (slug IN\" not in row[0]:\n        return\n    conn.execute(\"ALTER TABLE pages RENAME TO pages_legacy\")\n    conn.executescript(PAGES_SCHEMA)\n    conn.execute(\n        f\"INSERT INTO pages ({_PAGE_COLUMNS}) \"\n        f\"SELECT {_PAGE_COLUMNS} FROM pages_legacy\"\n    )\n    conn.execute(\"DROP TABLE pages_legacy\")\n\n\ndef get_connection(path: Path | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(path or settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    return conn\n\n\ndef init_db(path: Path | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Create the schema and, only on a brand-new database, seed the\n    starting Pages. Pages are freely creatable/deletable (see PAGE_SLUGS'\n    docstring), so this must not resurrect a page the Manager deleted —\n    it only bootstraps an empty table, never re-inserts into a populated one.\n    \"\"\"\n    conn = get_connection(path)\n    try:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n        if conn.execute(\"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pages\").fetchone()[0] == 0:\n            for slug in PAGE_SLUGS:\n                conn.execute(\n                    \"INSERT INTO pages (slug, title) VALUES (?, ?)\",\n                    (slug, PAGE_TITLES[slug]),\n                )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef create_user(email: str, password: str, role: str, *, active: bool = True) -> None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO users (email, password_hash, role, active) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (email, auth.hash_password(password), role, int(active)),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef get_user_by_email(email: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?\", (email,)\n        ).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef get_user_by_id(user_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?\", (user_id,)\n        ).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef set_active(email: str, *, active: bool) -> None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE users SET active = ? WHERE email = ?\", (int(active), email)\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef get_page_by_slug(slug: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM pages WHERE slug = ?\", (slug,)\n        ).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef list_pages() -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM pages ORDER BY slug\").fetchall()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef update_page(slug: str, *, title: str, body_md: str, status: str, author_id: int) -> None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"\"\"UPDATE pages\n               SET title = ?, body_md = ?, status = ?, author_id = ?,\n                   updated_at = datetime('now')\n               WHERE slug = ?\"\"\",\n            (title, body_md, status, author_id, slug),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef slug_is_valid(slug: str) -> bool:\n    return re.fullmatch(SLUG_PATTERN, slug) is not None\n\n\ndef create_page(slug: str, *, title: str, body_md: str, status: str, author_id: int) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Insert a new page. Returns False if the slug is already taken.\"\"\"\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO pages (slug, title, body_md, status, author_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (slug, title, body_md, status, author_id),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n        return True\n    except sqlite3.IntegrityError:\n        return False\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef delete_page(slug: str) -> None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM pages WHERE slug = ?\", (slug,))\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":85,"oldLines":6,"newStart":85,"newLines":7,"lines":["     conn = get_connection(path)","     try:","         conn.executescript(SCHEMA)","+        _migrate_legacy_page_slug_check(conn)","         if conn.execute(\"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pages\").fetchone()[0] == 0:","             for slug in PAGE_SLUGS:","                 conn.execute("]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"748a1b5d-ca4b-4595-8db3-aaa8616523b6","session_id":"a2316d11-3941-4d87-98fe-7d21dea1d9fa","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"2fa5b7df-506f-4d8e-a53d-7174fd72d15b","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"main"}

import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\n\nfrom app import db\n\n\ndef _csrf(client, path):\n    response = client.get(path)\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n    return response.cookies[\"csrf_token\"]\n\n\ndef test_manager_can_edit_a_permanent_page(client_as):\n    manager = client_as(\"admin\")\n    csrf = _csrf(manager, \"/admin/pages/home\")\n    response = manager.post(\n        \"/admin/pages/home\",\n        data={\n            \"title\": \"Home\",\n            \"body_md\": \"Visit us at Monte Everest 780, Lomas de Chapultepec.\",\n            \"status\": \"published\",\n            \"csrf_token\": csrf,\n        },\n    )\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n    page = db.get_page_by_slug(\"home\")\n    assert page[\"status\"] == \"published\"\n    assert \"Monte Everest 780\" in page[\"body_md\"]\n    assert page[\"author_id\"] is not None\n\n\ndef test_editor_is_blocked_from_edit_form(client_as):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    response = editor.get(\"/admin/pages/home\", follow_redirects=False)\n    assert response.status_code == 403\n\n\ndef test_editor_is_blocked_from_pages_list(client_as):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    response = editor.get(\"/admin/pages\", follow_redirects=False)\n    assert response.status_code == 403\n\n\ndef test_editor_is_blocked_from_a_direct_post(client_as):\n    \"\"\"A forged POST with no prior UI visit must still be rejected by role,\n    not merely by a missing CSRF token.\"\"\"\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    response = editor.post(\n        \"/admin/pages/home\",\n        data={\"title\": \"Hijacked\", \"body_md\": \"x\", \"status\": \"published\",\n              \"csrf_token\": \"not-even-a-real-token\"},\n        follow_redirects=False,\n    )\n    assert response.status_code == 403\n    assert db.get_page_by_slug(\"home\")[\"title\"] != \"Hijacked\"\n\n\ndef test_anonymous_is_redirected_to_login(client):\n    response = client.get(\"/admin/pages/home\", follow_redirects=False)\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    assert follow_redirects=False,\n    )\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    assert response.headers[\"location\"].endswith(\"/login\")\n\n\ndef test_saved_markdown_is_sanitized(client_as):\n    manager = client_as(\"admin\")\n    csrf = _csrf(manager, \"/admin/pages/menu\")\n    payload = '<script>alert(1)</script><img src=x onerror=\"alert(2)\">Tacos al pastor'\n    response = manager.post(\n        \"/admin/pages/menu\",\n        data={\"title\": \"Menu\", \"body_md\": payload, \"status\": \"draft\", \"csrf_token\": csrf},\n    )\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n\n assert \"<script\" not in response.text\n    assert \"onerror\" not in response.text\n\n\ndef test_saving_plain_text_does_not_corrupt_it(client_as):\n    \"\"\"Regression: sanitizing raw Markdown must \"status\": \"draft\", \"csrf_token\": csrf},\n    )\n    page = db.get_page_by_slug(\"menu\")\n    assert page[\"body_md\"] == 'Tacos & salsa, \"al pastor\"'\n\n\ndef data={\"slug\": \"events\", \"title\": \"Events\", \"body_md\": \"Coming soon.\",\n              \"status\": \"draft\", \"csrf_token\": csrf},\n        follow_redirects=False,\n    )\n    assert Pages are freely creatable/deletable (see PAGE_SLUGS'\n    docstring), so this must not resurrect a page the Manager deleted —\n    it only bootstraps an empty table, never re-inserts into a populated one.\n    \"\"\"\n    conn = get_connection(path)\n    try:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n        _migrate_legacy_page_slug_check(conn)\n        if conn.execute(\"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pages\").fetchone()[0] == 0:\n            for slug in PAGE_SLUGS:\n                conn.execute(\n                    \"INSERT INTO pages (slug, title) VALUES (?, ?)\",\n                    (slug, PAGE_TITLES[slug]),\n                )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()","newString":"def init_db(path: Path | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Create the schema and, only the first time the `pages` table is\n    created, seed the starting Pages. Pages are freely creatable/deletable\n    (see PAGE_SLUGS' docstring) and `init_db` runs again on every `cms serve`\n    restart, so this keys off whether the table already existed — not\n    whether it's currently empty — or deleting every page would make the\n    next restart look identical to a brand-new database and recreate them.\n    \"\"\"\n    conn = get_connection(path)\n    try:\n        table_already_existed = conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'pages'\"\n        ).fetchone() is not None\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n        _migrate_legacy_page_slug_check(conn)\n        if not table_already_existed:\n            for slug in PAGE_SLUGS:\n                conn.execute(\n                    \"INSERT INTO pages (slug, title) VALUES (?, ?)\",\n                    (slug, PAGE_TITLES[slug]),\n                )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()","originalFile":"\"\"\"SQLite connection and the users table.\n\nOne file, gitignored, rebuilt by `scripts/seed_demo.py`. See ADR-002 for why\nthere is no ORM here.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom app import auth, settings\n\n# La Once Mil's initial Pages (see notes/restaurant-research.md); this is\n# seed content, not a limit. Per the MP2 rubric/manual (\"Pages: same fields\n# and operations as posts, plus public navigation\"), Pages support full\n# create/read/update/delete like Posts — the Manager can add or remove pages\n# beyond this starting set.\nPAGE_SLUGS = (\"home\", \"menu\", \"our-story\")\nPAGE_TITLES = {\"home\": \"Home\", \"menu\": \"Menu\", \"our-story\": \"Our Story\"}\n\nUSERS_SCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,\n    role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1\n);\n\"\"\"\n\nPAGES_SCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pages (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    title TEXT NOT NULL,\n    body_md TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')) DEFAULT 'draft',\n    author_id INTEGER REFERENCES users(id),\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n);\n\"\"\"\n\nSCHEMA = USERS_SCHEMA + PAGES_SCHEMA\n\nSLUG_PATTERN = \"^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$\"\n\n_PAGE_COLUMNS = \"id, slug, title, body_md, status, author_id, created_at, updated_at\"\n\n\ndef _migrate_legacy_page_slug_check(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A database created before Pages supported full CRUD has\n    `CHECK (slug IN ('home', 'menu', 'our-story'))` baked into the `pages`\n    table — `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` never touches an existing table, so\n    that CHECK would otherwise survive forever and silently block creating\n    any other page. Rebuild the table from PAGES_SCHEMA, keeping every row.\n    \"\"\"\n    row = conn.execute(\n        \"SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'pages'\"\n    ).fetchone()\n    if row is None or row[0] is None or \"CHECK (slug IN\" not in row[0]:\n        return\n    conn.execute(\"ALTER TABLE pages RENAME TO pages_legacy\")\n    conn.executescript(PAGES_SCHEMA)\n    conn.execute(\n        f\"INSERT INTO pages ({_PAGE_COLUMNS}) \"\n        f\"SELECT {_PAGE_COLUMNS} FROM pages_legacy\"\n    )\n    conn.execute(\"DROP TABLE pages_legacy\")\n\n\ndef get_connection(path: Path | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(path or settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    return conn\n\n\ndef init_db(path: Path | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Create the schema and, only on a brand-new database, seed the\n    starting Pages. Pages are freely creatable/deletable (see PAGE_SLUGS'\n    docstring), so this must not resurrect a page the Manager deleted —\n    it only bootstraps an empty table, never re-inserts into a populated one.\n    \"\"\"\n    conn = get_connection(path)\n    try:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n        _migrate_legacy_page_slug_check(conn)\n        if conn.execute(\"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pages\").fetchone()[0] == 0:\n            for slug in PAGE_SLUGS:\n                conn.execute(\n                    \"INSERT INTO pages (slug, title) VALUES (?, ?)\",\n                    (slug, PAGE_TITLES[slug]),\n                )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef create_user(email: str, password: str, role: str, *, active: bool = True) -> None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO users (email, password_hash, role, active) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (email, auth.hash_password(password), role, int(active)),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef get_user_by_email(email: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?\", (email,)\n        ).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef get_user_by_id(user_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?\", (user_id,)\n        ).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef set_active(email: str, *, active: bool) -> None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE users SET active = ? WHERE email = ?\", (int(active), email)\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef get_page_by_slug(slug: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM pages WHERE slug = ?\", (slug,)\n        ).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef list_pages() -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM pages ORDER BY slug\").fetchall()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef update_page(slug: str, *, title: str, body_md: str, status: str, author_id: int) -> None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"\"\"UPDATE pages\n               SET title = ?, body_md = ?, status = ?, author_id = ?,\n                   updated_at = datetime('now')\n               WHERE slug = ?\"\"\",\n            (title, body_md, status, author_id, slug),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef slug_is_valid(slug: str) -> bool:\n    return re.fullmatch(SLUG_PATTERN, slug) is not None\n\n\ndef create_page(slug: str, *, title: str, body_md: str, status: str, author_id: int) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Insert a new page. Returns False if the slug is already taken.\"\"\"\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO pages (slug, title, body_md, status, author_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (slug, title, body_md, status, author_id),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n        return True\n    except sqlite3.IntegrityError:\n        return False\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef delete_page(slug: str) -> None:\n    conn = get_connection()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM pages WHERE slug = ?\", (slug,))\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":77,"oldLines":16,"newStart":77,"newLines":21,"lines":[" "," "," def init_db(path: Path | None = None) -> None:","-    \"\"\"Create the schema and, only on a brand-new database, seed the","-    starting Pages. Supersedes the earlier \"Tacos La Oncemil\" spelling used before this session, which was not an intentional name choice. |\n9\t| **Flagship location** | The one restaurant location this project models: Monte Everest 780, Lomas de Chapultepec, Mexico City — the Michelin-starred address. Editor drafts; admin publishes. |\n14\t| **Publish** | The admin-only action that marks a draft (News post or a permanent page edit) as published **in the local CMS**. The editor role cannot perform this action under any content type. Publishing is not the same as the public site updating — the GitHub Pages site only reflects the change after `cms publish` exports to `site/` and that export is deployed. |\n15\t| **Navigation reachability** | Every published page, including Home, must be reachable by clicking through the public site's navigation — no published page is an orphan with no link pointing to it. |\n16\t| **Visiting information** | Verified address, hours, a directions link, and a prominent Call button — lives entirely on Home. There is no separate Visit Us page. |\n17\t| **Menu (page)** | One ordinary Markdown permanent page listing dish names and descriptions. No prices (no verified peso pricing exists) and no structured menu/pricing database — deliberately out of scope. |\n18\t| **Placeholder image** | A clearly labeled stand-in image (e.g. `[PLACEHOLDER: storefront photo]`) used until a real, rights-cleared photo is supplied. Tracked in `notes/client-brief.md`'s image tracker. Never substituted with AI-generated or stock images. |\n19\t| **Michelin item** | The one real, dated news item seed content may include — the Michelin star announcement — because the Michelin Guide page directly confirms the exact distinction (\"One MICHELIN Star\") and attributes it to the flagship (Lomas de Chapultepec) address specifically. See `notes/client-brief.md`\nand `notes/restaurant-research.md` for the sourcing and reasoning behind each decision.\n\n| Term | Meaning in this project |\n|---|---|\n| **La Once Mil** | The site's display name — the restaurant's own verified branding. Supersedes the earlier \"Tacos La Oncemil\" spelling used before this session, which was not an intentional name choice. |\n| **Flagship location** | The one restaurant location this project models: Monte Everest 780, Lomas de Chapultepec, Mexico City — the Michelin-starred address. Roma Norte and Madrid locations are explicitly out of scope and must never appear on the site. |\n| **Demo Manager** | The seeded **admin** account for grading. Fictional — does not represent the real owner (César de la Parra) or any real staff. Can edit permanent pages, manage users, and publish. |\n| **Demo Editor** | The seeded **editor** account for grading. Fictional. Can create and edit **News** drafts only — cannot publish, cannot edit permanent pages, cannot manage users. |\n| **Permanent pages** | Home, Menu, and Our Story — the site's \"Pages\" capability. Admin-only to edit. Appear in public navigation (except Home, which is implicit). |\n| **News** | The site's \"Posts\" capability — draft/published announcements with title, slug, Markdown body, author, timestamps. Editor drafts; admin publishes. |\n| **Publish** | The admin-only action that marks a draft (News post or a permanent page edit) as published **in the local CMS**. The editor role cannot perform this action under any content type. Publishing is not the same as the public site updating — the GitHub Pages site only reflects the change after `cms publish` exports to `site/` and that export is deployed. |\n| **Navigation reachability** | Every published page, including Home, must be reachable by clicking through the public site's navigation — no published page is an orphan with no link pointing to it. |\n| **Visiting information** | Verified address, hours, a directions link, and a prominent Call button — lives entirely on Home. There is no separate Visit Us page. |\n| **Menu (page)** | One ordinary Markdown permanent page listing dish names and descriptions. No prices (no verified peso pricing exists) and no structured menu/pricing database — deliberately out of scope. |\n| **Placeholder image** | A clearly labeled stand-in image (e.g. `[PLACEHOLDER: storefront photo]`) used until a real, rights-cleared photo is supplied. Tracked in `notes/client-brief.md`'s image tracker. Never substituted with AI-generated or stock images. |\n| **Michelin item** | The one real, dated news item seed content may include — the Michelin star announcement — because the Michelin Guide page directly confirms the exact distinction (\"One MICHELIN Star\") and attributes it to the flagship (Lomas de Chapultepec) address specifically. This is a class prototype modeling a hypothetical future\n  hire, not real restaurant staff.","originalFile":"# Client brief: La Once Mil, Lomas de Chapultepec, Mexico City\n\n## Why this client\n\nI picked this restaurant because the Michelin-star story is compelling: a taqueria — a\ncategory of restaurant normally associated with cheap, fast street food — won a Michelin\nstar in 2026, the only taquería to hold that distinction. That tension (a $20 wagyu taco next\nto a genre built on $1 street tacos) is a strong hook for a \"what can I eat here, where is it,\nwhen is it open\" public site, and the restaurant's real story (chef César de la Parra\ndeliberately elevating a street-food format he grew up on) gives the \"Our Story\" page\nsomething specific to say instead of generic restaurant copy.\n\n**Scope note:** this project models only the flagship location — Monte Everest 780, Lomas\nde Chapultepec — the Michelin-starred address. The restaurant also operates a second Mexico\nCity branch (Roma Norte) and, as of very recently (Sept 2026), a Madrid location; both are\nexplicitly out of scope. See `notes/restaurant-research.md` for full sourcing and the\nnaming decision (site uses \"La Once Mil,\" the restaurant's own verified branding; an\nearlier draft of this brief used \"Tacos La Oncemil,\" which was corrected on 2026-09-28).\n\n## Who runs the site, and how comfortable are they with computers?\n\n**Proposed assumption, not a verified fact** (I have not contacted the restaurant): the site\nis modeled as run by the owner, César de la Parra, posting everything himself. He's a working\nchef running a 55-seat, ~80-staff restaurant — comfortable enough to run Instagram and\nTikTok accounts personally, but with no patience for a complicated publishing workflow. He\nneeds to post fast between service, not fight with a CMS. This means the editor UI has to be\nsimple even though, today, there's only one real user.\n\nThe CMS still needs two enforced roles (admin/editor) per the assignment's fixed\nrequirements — the brief models a plausible future where a manager or social-media hire gets\nan editor account without touching user management, permanent-page content (Home, Menu, Our\nStory — which includes the address/hours/directions on Home), or publishing.\n\n## Who reads it, and what are they usually trying to find?\n\nTwo kinds of visitors, inferred from the restaurant's real profile (no reservations, walk-in\nonly, high foot traffic from the Michelin attention, no functioning official website today):\n\n- **First-time visitors drawn by the Michelin coverage**, wanting to know: what's the\n  signature dish, what does it cost, where exactly is it, when is it open, is a reservation\n  needed (no).\n- **Repeat/local visitors** wanting quick answers: today's hours, any seasonal menu news,\n  confirmation the place hasn't moved.\n\n## What's broken about how they do it now?\n\nVerified from research: the restaurant has no functioning official website (`laoncemil.com`\nexists but shows only \"under construction\"). Its entire online presence is Instagram,\nTikTok, and a Linktree — none of which answer \"where and when\" quickly, and all of which bury\nthat information under a scrolling feed. Someone who doesn't already follow the account has\nno fast way to get the address and hours without digging through an Instagram bio.\n\n## What would make them say \"this is better\"?\n\nA page that says, in one glance: what the signature dishes are, that it's walk-in only\n(setting the right expectation before someone shows up expecting to book), the exact address\nand hours, and a way to see it's a real, currently-open, currently-relevant place (recent\nannouncements) without needing to already follow the Instagram.\n\n## What must not happen\n\n**This site must never imply that Tacos La Oncemil / La Once Mil commissioned, endorsed, or\nwas involved in building this project.** It is a student prototype built for a class\nassignment using publicly available, verified information. Any demonstration content (sample\nannouncements, seed data) must be clearly labeled as such, not presented as if the restaurant\nposted it.\n\n## Confirmed decisions (2026-09-28, in `/grill-with-docs`)\n\n- **Site display name is \"La Once Mil\"** — the restaurant's own verified branding.\n  (Corrects the earlier \"Tacos La Oncemil\" spelling used when this brief was started;\n  that was not an intentional name choice. See `notes/restaurant-research.md`.)\n- **Publishing is admin-only.** Only the manager/admin role can publish content live;\n  the demo editor can create and edit announcement drafts but cannot publish, cannot\n  edit permanent pages (Home, Menu, Our Story), and cannot manage users. The\n  admin can do everything. This is a class prototype modeling a hypothetical future\n  hire, not real restaurant staff.\n- **Demo accounts are fictional, not the real owner.** Seed users are named\n  **\"Demo Manager\"** (admin) and **\"Demo Editor\"** (editor) — required to demonstrate\n  both roles for grading, but explicitly not claiming to be César de la Parra or any\n  real staff member.\n- **Homepage priority order: address, hours, directions first.** Of the \"what/where/when\"\n  facts a first-time visitor needs, address/hours/directions rank above signature-dish\n  or walk-in-only copy on the homepage specifically (those still belong on the page,\n  just not the top fold).\n- **Contact method is phone only.** No contact form, no email address surfaced to\n  customers — a phone number is the one channel offered for reaching the restaurant.\n- **Menu is one ordinary Markdown page** (dish names and descriptions), not a\n  structured menu/pricing database. No unverified peso prices are included, per\n  `notes/restaurant-research.md`'s pricing caveat.\n- **News/announcements may include one real, dated item** — the Michelin star\n  announcement, since the Michelin Guide page directly confirms the exact distinction\n  (\"One MICHELIN Star\") and attributes it to the Lomas de Chapultepec address\n  specifically (see `notes/restaurant-research.md`). Any other seed announcements are\n  invented sample content and must be clearly labeled as demo, not real restaurant\n  posts.\n- **Images: placeholders now, real photos intended for the final version.** Build\n  proceeds today with clearly labeled placeholders (e.g. `[PLACEHOLDER: storefront\n  photo]`) so nothing blocks on photo access. See \"Image tracker\" below for what's\n  still needed before final.\n\n## Image tracker (placeholders in use until these are supplied)\n\n| Needed for | Status | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Homepage hero image | Placeholder | Storefront or signature dish shot, Lomas de Chapultepec location only |\n| Menu page image(s) | Placeholder | Food shots; no prices, per pricing caveat |\n| Our Story image | Placeholder | Chef/kitchen or storefront shot |\n| News/announcement images (optional, per post) | Placeholder | Only if a specific post needs one |\n\nPer `notes/restaurant-research.md`: the three photos found in the Michelin article are\ncredited \"© La Once Mil\" (editorial credit, not a republishing license) and are **not\ncleared for use**. Real photos must come from the user's own Instagram pulls (with\npost date/caption/credit noted) or the user's own photography — not these Michelin\narticle images, and not AI-generated or stock substitutes.\n\n## Page structure (2026-09-28, in `/grill-with-docs`)\n\n- **Home covers visiting information entirely** — verified address, hours, a\n  directions link, and a prominent Call button live on Home itself.
